summary: TechCrunch reports that Gaza's growing tech sector, which served international firms like Nvidia and hosted the Alphabet-backed Gaza Sky Geeks, has been crippled by Israel's bombardment after Hamas's attacks on Israel. Infrastructure, universities, offices and internet and electricity access have been destroyed or cut off, while the West Bank ecosystem also slowed. Founders and tech workers describe danger, repeated evacuations and an uncertain future for the industry.
one_line: Israel's bombardment of Gaza after Hamas's attacks has devastated Palestine's nascent tech industry, destroying infrastructure, universities and connectivity and halting work.
key_facts: Nvidia has worked for years with at least 100 engineers from Gaza; the outsourcing initiative was driven by Mellanox founder Eyal Waldman, whose daughter was murdered in the Hamas attacks.
Those working in the region estimate as much as $10 million has been invested in the Palestinian tech ecosystem to date.
In 2017, Salesforce founder and CEO Marc Benioff and other Silicon Valley figures backed the first coding academy in Gaza.
Gaza Sky Geeks, an Alphabet-backed initiative run with Mercy Corps, is the largest tech hub in Palestine; in 2022, 5,000 coders and developers from the West Bank and Gaza graduated from its program.
Hamas kidnapped at least 150 people and killed 1,300 people in Israel; over 1,500 people in Palestine had been killed in Israel's retaliation at the time of writing.

Ryan Sturgill, former head of Gaza Sky Geeks, said the area around the Mercy Corps building was leveled, the fiber lines and offices destroyed, and the three main universities producing computer science grads in Gaza were leveled.
Ibtikar, a main Palestinian VC fund, had recently raised its second fund of $30 million.
Iliana Montauk of Manara said electricity was cut off across Gaza, both ISPs and many buildings holding cell towers were bombed, and people get only about 10 minutes of warning to evacuate.
Manara has around 100 software engineers in Gaza, some working remotely for tech companies in Silicon Valley and Europe.
Dalia Awad, whose 2021 Medium post about getting into Google from Gaza went viral, reported only 2G cellular data and WhatsApp messaging during the bombing.
Leen Abubaker of Flow Accelerator said West Bank tech activity has frozen, with roads blocked by Israeli forces and settlers, and that Burj Al-Watan in Gaza was destroyed.
Mohammad Alnobani, founder of The Middle Frame, was stuck in Jordan after borders closed while returning from the One Young World Summit in Belfast.
About 1.1 million people in northern Gaza were told to leave as Israel massed soldiers ahead of an expected ground offensive and enforced a total blockade.
